one_liner: Devin has a documented v3 REST API (sessions, playbooks, knowledge, enterprise) using cog_ bearer tokens and an official MCP server. API access seems to need a paid self-serve plan, and the Free plan's API access is unclear.
auth_notes: Service user API keys and personal access tokens, both cog_-prefixed bearer tokens. No OAuth2 app flow is documented. Legacy apk_ keys are deprecated.
access_notes: Self-serve plans are Free, Pro $20/mo, Max $200/mo and Teams $80/mo. The pricing table has a "Devin API" row, but the snippet doesn't show which plans include it. The Free plan description does not list API access, so a paid plan is assumed. Enterprise deployments use a custom API domain.
blocker_notes: The builder likely needs a paid plan (Pro $20/mo) to get API credentials. The snippets don't confirm whether the Free plan includes the API. Multi-user access relies on per-user PATs or service keys, not OAuth.

evidence.quote: All API credentials use the `cog_` prefix format. Include your token in the `Authorization` header of every request
Personal Access Tokens (PATs) allow human users to authenticate programmatically under their own identity.
The Free plan lets you try Devin with limited usage. It includes: - Limited Devin usage - Access to [Devin Review](/work-with-devin/devin-review)
Go to **Settings > Devin API** in your organization and open the **Service users** tab
The Devin API enables you to integrate Devin into your applications, automate workflows, and build powerful tools.
The Devin MCP server is an authenticated service that provides access to both public and private repositories, plus full platform management capabilities.
